mpu.note: ISP model is omitted because the manual names both Spectra 690 and Spectra 692.

limited_rails.note: The manual does not clarify whether the stated limit applies independently to each rail.

jmedia_logic.note: Logic-domain statement only; the connector also carries VIN and 3.3 V power pins.

VIN.note: UNO VIN input; 1.1 A PTC fuse; see voltage.uno_vin_input.

QWIIC_SCL.note: Controller designation conflicts with the Qwiic section.

QWIIC_SDA.note: Controller designation conflicts with the Qwiic section.

JMISC_59.note: MPU and MCU RTC backup only; not board backup power.

QWIIC_I2C.note: PA8 and PC9 follow the Communication / I2C table; I2C3 versus I2C4 naming is unresolved.

UNO_CAN.note: These are MCU logic signals, not the transceiver bus terminals.

CAN_BUS.note: PD0/PD1 TX/RX assignments conflict in the manual and are not resolved here.

HDMI.note: HDMI and JMEDIA MIPI-DSI cannot be active simultaneously.

JCTL.note: Pin positions and logic levels are not specified in the local manual text.

rgb_leds.note: MCU port mappings are not given in the manual text.

multiplexing.note: Listed alternate functions are not a guarantee of simultaneous availability.

expansion.camera_support_note: Support statement belongs to the manual snapshot, not an exhaustive hardware compatibility claim.

physical.uno_shield_compatibility: Mechanical and pin compatibility only; software compatibility is not established.

unspecified: UNO header input tolerance and per-pin current limits are not established by the local manual text.
No global logic voltage is assigned because connectors span multiple voltage domains.

source.author: Karl Söderby
source.scope: Transcription of the local manual; linked PDFs were not used to resolve discrepancies.
source.pin_naming: UNO analog pins use A0-A5 with D14-D19 aliases, following the Uno R3 definition. Expansion keys use CONNECTOR_position, with physical_pin scoped to connector. maps_to preserves each expansion table's signal label; mcu_pin or source_function preserves its separate port or function column when supplied.
coverage_gaps: Complete UNO power-header positions, Qwiic positions, JCTL pinout, and camera pinouts are not provided in the manual text.
MCU package pin numbers, board revision, and per-pin electrical limits are not specified.
High-speed and carrier signal labels are transcribed as published, without schematic verification.

claims: I2C3 on PA8 and PC9 in the I2C table
discrepancies.disposition: Keep PA8 and PC9 from the explicit table; omit a definitive controller number.

claims: CAN Interfaces lists PD0 as TX and PD1 as RX.
The transceiver table lists PD1 at TXD and PD0 at RXD; the terminal table follows that assignment.
discrepancies.disposition: Keep CAN-H/CAN-L as bus signals; omit definitive MCU TX/RX routing for the onboard transceiver.
Record both source claims without selecting a version.

claims: Architecture and camera sections name Spectra 692
Wireless Connectivity calls it dual-band while listing 2.4/5/6 GHz
discrepancies.disposition: Preserve the three stated bands without adopting the band-count wording.

claims: The ten-bit example comment says 0 to 4095
discrepancies.disposition: Omit the inconsistent example range; retain the documented eight-bit default.

reset.warning: Disabling RESET prevents ordinary low-voltage ISP programming. High-voltage programming may be required to recover the device.

conversion.note: Speed of sound varies with temperature and environmental conditions.

source.variant_warning: Specifications can vary between HC-SR04 manufacturers and revisions.
